To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified the zebrafisht mutant gene cdy, which encodes divalent-metal transporter 1, and demonstrated the conservation of iron transport in vertebrates.
we have used zebrafish to identify the vertebrate iron transporter divalent-metal transporter 1 (dmt1) and demonstrate that the dmt1 gene is essential for normal erythropoiesic function.

we have identified a nonsense mutation that disrupts the divalent metal transporter gene (DMT1 or Nramp2) in a zebrafis mutant, chardonnay, and that this mutation leads to a defect in iron uptake in both the intestine and red blood cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of iron deficiency and overload in vertebrates and the development of zebrafish models of iron deficiency and iron overload.
the identification of genes that are involved in iron metabolism.
the identification and characterization of a new zebrafish gene that is involved in iron metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the zebrafis cdy mutant is a model for iron deficiency anemia.
the chardonnay mutant is a loss of function mutation in the zebrafisch DMT1 gene.
this is the first report of a DMT1 mutation in any organism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a zebrafisht mutant with a microcytic anemic phenotype and demonstrated that it is caused by a mutation in the gene encoding DMT1.
we identified a zebrafis mutant that is defective in the iron transporter DMT1, which causes anemia.
DMT1 is required for the absorption and utilization of dietary iron and is essential for normal red blood cell development.
